task.title: Desktop WKWebView popovers misposition: the JS anchor fallback is broken
task.description:
Maintainer screenshots (2026-08-16, release .app on macOS): both original popover symptoms reproduce in the DESKTOP app — the tray's Move-to destination picker renders below the window (thin sliver visible at the bottom edge), and the catalog 'Adding to' picker shows the slim gray bar above the trigger. Both were fixed by #148 and verified green on Chromium and Playwright's WebKit 26.5 — engines WITH CSS anchor positioning. The system WKWebView the Tauri shell embeds evidently lacks anchor positioning on this macOS build, so the css::supports-gated JS fallback (popover.rs position_below_trigger) is live there — and it carries the two flaws consciously dropped when it was dead code (adversarial review of #148, minors): it always places the panel BELOW the trigger and left-aligned (off-screen for the bottom-docked tray; ignores PopoverAlign::End) and never clamps to viewport edges. The #148 ResizeObserver fix addressed stale height only, not placement.

To do: (1) confirm empirically that the installed WKWebView lacks anchor positioning (drive the .app or a WKWebView harness; CSS.supports('anchor-name: --a') is the probe — record macOS/WebKit version); (2) make the fallback honor PopoverAlign (End/Center), flip above/below by available space, and clamp to viewport edges — the CSS path's semantics, in JS; (3) verify per surface: tray Move-to picker (bottom-docked → must open ABOVE), catalog Adding-to (Center), tree-manage pickers, user menu, hover previews (hover_card shares the caveat per the gap analysis); (4) e2e where honest: the suite is chromium-only and chromium has anchors, so in-suite tests can't exercise the fallback — a one-off webkit-with-anchors-disabled or JS-forced-fallback probe script is the verification vehicle (precedent: #148's isolated repro stripped anchor declarations); state what's automatable vs maintainer click-through. Screenshots referenced: Desktop/Screenshot 2026-08-16 11.28.53 AM (tray) and the 11.29.00 capture (Adding to).
